description: Converge the Session read-side: unify transcript closure event naming to a single dot-token, collapse duplicated transcript-loading and context-ref assembly into shared helpers, decompose AgentSessionQuerier into independent usage-reporter and activity-feed services, and delete zero-call dead DTO code. Pure refactor, zero observable behavior change.

tasks.title: Unify transcript closure event naming to the dot-separated token session.closed
tasks.description: Flip TranscriptPartTypes.SessionClosed from "session_closed" to "session.closed" (aligning with RuntimeEventTypes.SessionClosed) and remove the underscore constant entirely. The write side (TranscriptAccumulator.ToTranscriptPartType) then persists closure parts with the dot type. Every read-side matcher is switched to the single constant and its dual-spelling / literal acceptance is removed: AgentSessionQuerier.ReadTerminalStateAsync (drop the `|| "session_closed"` branch), LoadTerminalFactsAsync, TerminalFact.FromTranscript, TranscriptEventSummaryProjector, SessionTranscriptBuilder, and AgentSessionSummaryBuilder (both literal sites). Literal-asserting specs are updated to expect session.closed.
acceptanceCriteria: TranscriptPartTypes.SessionClosed equals "session.closed" and no constant with value "session_closed" exists in that class
RuntimeEventTypes.SessionClosed and TranscriptPartTypes.SessionClosed carry the same string value
TranscriptAccumulator.ToTranscriptPartType maps the session.closed runtime event to a part whose Type is session.closed
rg over packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/ for the literal "session_closed" returns zero type-comparison hits (doc comments referencing the historical name are not type comparisons)
ReadTerminalStateAsync filters closure parts by session.closed only with no || underscore alternative
Literal-asserting specs (AgentSessionSpecs, AgentSessionReadApiSpecs, GenericAgentSessionSummarySpecs, AgentJobGrainSpecs) updated to session.closed and pass
`npm test` (server) is green with TreatWarningsAsErrors; all existing Session specs pass with no regression
tasks.output: Unified closure-event vocabulary across emit/accumulate/persist/read paths; updated literal-asserting specs
tasks.notes: Stage 1 of the design migration plan — isolated, lowest blast radius, do first. Under AGENTS.md no-version-compat stance, historical session_closed rows losing terminal resolution on read is an accepted dev-only non-issue (no backfill by default).

tasks.title: Collapse transcript loading and context-ref construction into single shared helpers
tasks.description: Introduce one internal static transcript loader (e.g. TranscriptPartLoader.LoadAsync(db, sessionIds, partTypeFilter?)) returning the sessionByTurnId map plus materialized parts, and rewire all five former duplication sites (LoadLatestEventsAsync, LoadEventSummariesAsync, LoadTerminalFactsAsync, GetGenericSessionSummaryAsync, BuildSessionMetadataDtoAsync inline projection) onto it — each call site keeps its own ordering key and last-wins reduction. Introduce one internal static context-ref parser (e.g. AgentSessionContextRefs.TryBuild) reading the four launch labels with null-when-all-empty semantics, returning a nullable value tuple; both BuildAgentSessionListContextRefs and BuildGenericSessionSummaryContextRefs delegate to it and map the tuple to their own distinct DTO. LoadTranscriptAsync (single-session) becomes a thin wrapper over the shared loader.
acceptanceCriteria: The turns -> turnIds -> parts -> sessionByTurnId-dictionary sequence appears exactly once in the codebase and all five former duplication sites call the shared loader

The four-label context-reference construction logic (read issue-number label, parse to int-or-null, read epic/repository/workspace labels, return null when all absent) appears exactly once and both the agent-scoped list and generic-session summary delegate to it
AgentSessionListContextRefsDto and GenericAgentSessionSummaryContextRefsDto remain distinct wire shapes (only construction logic is shared)
Latest-event, event-summary, and terminal-fact loading produce per-session dictionaries identical to pre-consolidation results (same ordering and last-wins semantics)
Generic-session summary and session-metadata transcript projections produce identical resolved model, counts, and event summary as before
contextRefs envelopes on AgentSessionListItemDto and GenericAgentSessionSummaryDto are identical to pre-consolidation values
`npm test` (server) is green; all existing Session-related specs pass with no regression
tasks.output: Single TranscriptPartLoader and AgentSessionContextRefs shared helpers; five load sites and two context-ref callers rewired
tasks.notes: Stage 2. Depends on T-001 because LoadTerminalFactsAsync is both a consolidation site and a closure-type filter site; unifying naming first means consolidation relocates already-final code and avoids touching the same lines twice. Loader returns raw materials (not pre-reduced) so each caller imposes its own ordering — preserves byte-identical results.

tasks.title: Extract AgentActivityFeedAssembler as an independent scoped service
tasks.description: Move GetActivityAsync and its private helpers (ToActivityCard, BuildTaskProgressMapAsync, LoadIssueTitlesAsync, latest-event/preview/truncate helpers) into a new sealed AgentActivityFeedAssembler under Sessions/Services/ implementing IScopedService. The assembler depends one-way on the core AgentSessionQuerier (for listing + ReconcileActiveSessionsAsync, which stays internal on the querier) and on the shared transcript loader from T-002; the core querier never depends back. The _workflowQuerier dependency moves from the core querier constructor to the assembler (it was only used by BuildTaskProgressMapAsync). Update the /activity route DI injection and any direct-construction unit spec (GenericAgentSessionSummarySpecs direct-construction site) for the changed core querier constructor signature.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentSessionQuerier no longer contains GetActivityAsync, ToActivityCard, BuildTaskProgressMapAsync, or any activity-feed-specific private helper
AgentActivityFeedAssembler is a sealed IScopedService under Sessions/Services/ and the /activity route resolves it via DI
Dependency direction is one-way: assembler -> core querier + shared loader, never back (compiler enforces no circular reference)
The /activity endpoint response (summary counts, session cards with usage/event-summary/work-item/task-progress projections, waiting cards) is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-split response
A row is added for AgentActivityFeedAssembler in MigratedServicesRegistrationSpecs.MigratedServices (Scoped lifetime)
Direct-construction unit spec(s) updated for the core querier constructor signature change (dropped _workflowQuerier arg)
`npm test` (server) is green; all existing Session-related specs pass with no regression
tasks.output: AgentActivityFeedAssembler scoped service; rewired /activity route; updated registration + direct-construction specs
tasks.notes: Stage 3. Depends on T-002 because the assembler consumes the shared transcript loader (design D2). IScopedService auto-registration means no manual AddScoped wiring; MigratedServicesRegistrationSpecs asserts self-registration with correct lifetime.

tasks.title: Extract AgentUsageReporter as an independent scoped service
tasks.description: Move GetUsageTimeseriesAsync, GetCostRollupAsync, GetCostWindowedAsync and their private aggregation helpers (pre-window spend, cumulative-cost-per-ship, completed-issue-count load, per-window figure build, UsageBucketData, HasUsage) into a new sealed AgentUsageReporter under Sessions/Services/ implementing IScopedService. Update the /usage and /cost (timeseries, rollup, windowed) route DI injection. Decide at implementation time whether shared DTO mappers (ToUsageDto/BuildUsageHistoryDto) stay as internal static on the core querier (reporter calls through) or move to a small shared mapper — either preserves behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentSessionQuerier no longer contains GetUsageTimeseriesAsync, GetCostRollupAsync, GetCostWindowedAsync, or any of their private cost-aggregation helpers
AgentUsageReporter is a sealed IScopedService under Sessions/Services/ and the /usage, /cost-rollup, and /cost-windowed routes resolve it via DI
The usage-timeseries response (buckets, cumulative-cost-per-ship points, range, currency resolution) is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-split response
The cost-rollup response (total-cost, today-cost) is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-split values
The cost-windowed response (current/previous-window spend and per-issue-cost, with independent emptiness evaluation per metric per window) is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-split values
A row is added for AgentUsageReporter in MigratedServicesRegistrationSpecs.MigratedServices (Scoped lifetime)
`npm test` (server) is green; all existing Session-related specs pass with no regression
tasks.output: AgentUsageReporter scoped service; rewired /usage and /cost routes; updated registration specs
tasks.notes: Stage 4. Sequenced after T-003 because both extractions heavily edit AgentSessionQuerier.cs; doing activity first keeps the file spec-green between steps. Core query, followup, and cancel methods (ResolveFollowupTargetAsync etc.) remain in the core querier — out of AC scope.
